 The Social Security Administration recently announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, increasing monthly benefits for nearly 72 million Social Security recipients.
 The adjustment will take effect in January 2027. On average, Social Security retirement benefits will increase by $75 per month, according to the agency.
 Payments for approximately 7.3 million people receiving Supplemental Security Income will reflect the increase beginning Dec. 31, 2026. Some individuals receive both Social Security benefits and Supplemental Security Income.
 “Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano said in the announcement.
 Beneficiaries with personal my Social Security accounts will be able to view their cost-of-living adjustment notices online beginning in late November, up to three weeks before paper notices arrive by mail.
 Account holders can also sign up for text or email alerts when new messages, including COLA notices, become available in their online Message Center.
 People who do not have an account must create one and enroll in paperless notices by Nov. 18 to access their COLA notice online. Those who have not enrolled in paperless notices will receive their notices by mail in December.
 The agency said the new notices will feature a simplified, one-page format with personalized language and details about each recipient’s updated benefit amount, payment dates and any deductions.
 Information about Medicare changes for 2027 will be available at Medicare.gov . Medicare enrollees will be able to view their 2027 premium amounts through the my Social Security Message Center beginning in late November.
 The annual cost-of-living adjustment is calculated under the Social Security Act and is tied to changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, as determined by the U.S. Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics.
 For more information about the 2027 adjustment, visit ssa.gov/cola .
